membership_review.reason: A learned baseline-to-future organ-image prediction is implemented and evaluated. Do not interpret diffusion-state persistence as clinical-state persistence.

criteria_met: The institution, collection period, patient-linked imaging inputs, tumor delineations, and survival information are identified.
Baseline and target MRI acquisition are distinguished relative to surgery and radiotherapy initiation.
The patient-level partition and dataset sample units are reported.
criteria_missing: Variable-level acquisition and information-availability timestamps are not documented as retained model-accessible provenance.
Scanner/protocol identifiers, physical voxel units, intensity transformations, and traceable registration or slice-correspondence transformations are not reported.
A versioned source-data or preprocessing provenance record is not described.
assertions.rationale: This is partial documentation of patient-linked source and temporal provenance, shared by the four LDM configurations. It does not establish a complete operational variable-level provenance service.

scope.time_horizon: Baseline MRI before radiotherapy to MRI acquired four months after radiotherapy began

assertions.rationale: The collection period and relative scan timing are reported, but retention or reversible availability of each patient's actual scan dates and baseline-to-target interval is not established. The nominal four-month target is not evidence of native timestamp retention.

The baseline-input configurations use pre-treatment MRI/GTV, with predicted survival added in pred 2-class. The paper does not describe information-release timestamps, delineation availability latency, or queries audited against those timestamps. The survival classifier's development partition is also unspecified.

The GTV mask identifies tumor location; it is not a missingness or measurement-validity indicator. No mechanism distinguishing missing or invalid MRI/GTV values from observed values is described. Selection of paired scans does not establish such a mechanism.

scope.time_horizon: One future MRI generated from a fixed baseline image/mask pair

assertions.applicability_reason: The documented inference operation has no carried-forward clinical measurements or asynchronously refreshed variables whose per-variable age must be updated. It consumes a fixed baseline MRI/GTV pair for one future-image query. This does not make actual scan timing or information-availability timing inapplicable.

scope.time_horizon: Nominal target four months after radiotherapy initiation

assertions.rationale: The algorithm does not expose real elapsed clinical time as an input. Actual interval variability and its handling are not reported, so uniform spacing with ignored known unequal intervals is not asserted. Diffusion indices, DDIM steps, and epochs do not establish irregular clinical-time handling.

The paper describes scan selection, scheduled follow-up, and tumor-containing slice inclusion, but not a model of when, whether, or why observations occur conditional on patient or acquisition state. Selection rules are not themselves a modeled observation-generation process.

No target-specific temporal witness-preservation experiment across sampled values, update/validity patterns, native timing, and external channels is reported. A four-month target and image-similarity evaluation do not establish an observation-clock audit or a clock regime.

The modality and 256×256 image matrix are identified, but no traceable mapping of source-specific measurement definitions, scanner protocols, physical units, or intensity scales to a declared target schema is reported. Equal latent dimensions concern tensor concatenation, not semantic or unit harmonization.

criteria_met: An 80%/10%/10% patient-level training/validation/test partition is reported.
The VQ-VAE and LDM test sets are explicitly identical.
This configuration does not receive a survival-class condition.
criteria_missing: Training-only fitting of all preprocessing and transformations is not documented.
An information-release audit for baseline inputs is not reported.
Image correspondence and selection procedures are not documented sufficiently for a complete leakage audit.
assertions.rationale: Patient-level separation is a substantive control, but it does not by itself establish every feature-availability and preprocessing condition. Classifier-partition uncertainty is not assigned to this no-class configuration.

A local single-center dataset and training hardware are described, but no federated participants, local training/query protocol, or exchanged artifacts are reported. Single-center provenance alone is not an explicit negative statement about federation and does not establish privacy controls.

criteria_met: A trained MRI VQ-VAE maps pre-treatment MRI slices into quantized latent representations.
A separate trained GTV VQ-VAE maps tumor masks into compatible latent representations.
These representations are operational conditioning inputs to the evaluated future-image generator.
assertions.rationale: The shared encoding responsibility is implemented in the four configurations. This does not establish a persistent clinical belief state, foundation-checkpoint reuse, or missing-modality robustness.

The paper reports trained MRI/GTV VQ-VAEs and a pretrained ResNet-based classifier learned on the same cohort, but identifies no transferred foundation-encoder checkpoint/version or adaptation protocol. An implementation based on Stable Diffusion does not establish transfer of Stable Diffusion encoder parameters. Conversely, training on this cohort does not explicitly establish training from scratch.

Absent for the described LDM training objective: Algorithm 1 minimizes error in predicting sampled Gaussian corruption noise, not error against a target patient/image representation predicted from context. The use of quantized latents and conditional denoising does not itself establish a JEPA-style representation-prediction objective. This conclusion concerns the specified LDM loss, not unreported auxiliary encoder losses.

No specified representation-collapse prevention term, constraint, proof, or collapse diagnostic is reported for these learned representations. The generic discussion of avoiding GAN mode collapse concerns a different phenomenon. A VQ-VAE codebook or the name of a cited method does not establish the actual anti-collapse training mechanism.

Absent specifically as an observed-image reconstruction loss in the supplied LDM training algorithm: its written objective compares predicted noise with sampled Gaussian noise. Decoding generated latents and computing image-similarity metrics at evaluation do not turn that objective into an observed-image reconstruction loss. This does not establish absence of reconstruction training in the separately trained autoencoders.

scope.time_horizon: One MRI target four months after radiotherapy initiation

criteria_met: Imaging representations and an actual clinical survival-outcome category jointly condition generation.
MRI/GTV latents enter concatenation; the survival-class embedding enters U-Net cross-attention.
assertions.rationale: This is implemented imaging–clinical-label fusion, not proof of a beneficial fusion effect. The ground-truth survival category is hindsight information, not a baseline-available clinical modality.

The paper describes MRI/GTV latent concatenation but no availability, quality, or recency conditioning and no missing-image or missing-GTV behavior. The designed omission of survival conditioning in this ablation is not an availability-aware inference mechanism.

scope.time_horizon: Baseline MRI to one four-month post-radiotherapy-start MRI target

assertions.rationale: A baseline representation is retained as conditioning, but the source does not clearly define it as an evolving clinical state carried into a subsequent clinical prediction/update. Recurrence of the noisy target latent is computational denoising, not clinical-state persistence. An explicit clinical predecessor/successor state interface would resolve the identity question.

The described baseline-state path encodes and quantizes MRI/GTV into conditioning tensors; it does not maintain a posterior/filtering distribution over hidden clinical state. Gaussian initialization and reverse diffusion generate future images and are not a maintained state belief. Absence is restricted to this documented inference mechanism.

The documented inference generates a future image from fixed baseline conditioning and contains no correction operation using a newly measured clinical observation. Reverse-diffusion denoising is not observation assimilation. This scoped absence is not a claim that a forecaster requires filtering.

scope.time_horizon: Fixed baseline to one future MRI

assertions.rationale: The complete described prediction uses one baseline MRI/GTV and does not receive later measured observations. No current patient state is sequentially updated during this inference operation.

Population training updates theta, whereas the supplied inference algorithm only applies the trained denoiser to patient inputs and updates the sampled target latent. It contains no individual parameter-fitting or weight-update rule. This absence is restricted to the described inference path.

The shared MRI VQ-VAE encodes pre/post image domains, but the paper does not establish one maintained state feeding at least two typed prediction tasks/readouts. Reconstruction scores and several metrics of the same generated image do not establish this feature.

criteria_met: A no-survival-condition configuration is compared against predicted and observed survival-conditioned configurations.
Whole-image and local future-image metrics are reported for the omitted conditioning variable.
assertions.rationale: This satisfies the narrow variable-ablation form of the definition, not proof of a sufficient persistent clinical state. It does not test omission of baseline anatomy, multi-visit history, or treatment determinants.

criteria_met: The individual's pre-target MRI and GTV explicitly condition the future-image forecast through encoded latent concatenation.
assertions.rationale: Presence is narrowly baseline-observation conditioning: one prior clinical timepoint relative to the forecast. It does not establish multi-visit history integration, extra temporal memory, persistent-state semantics, or a measured personalization advantage.

No matched baseline-image/GTV swap, withholding, or population-prior control tests the value of the correct individual's information. Removing survival conditioning leaves individual anatomy intact and is not that audit.

Baseline MRI/GTV conditioning is intended to guide structure and tumor location, but no identity/anatomy-preserving memory, constraint, or loss is specified. Shared encoding and reconstruction quality do not establish the required transition-consistency mechanism.

MRI and the input GTV have recognizable semantics, but the learned quantized state codes have no reported entity/physiology mapping or state-inspection procedure. Viewing decoded images is not by itself inspectable latent-state semantics.

The described model uses one supplied baseline MRI/GTV rather than a history beyond that snapshot. The complete inference contains no clinical recurrent memory, visit context, or historical action sequence. Denoising iteration state is not extra clinical history memory.

The documented no-class inputs are MRI/GTV conditioning and target-generation noise. No treatment choice, dose, schedule, or executable command enters the prediction. Being paired before/after observed care does not make treatment a settable model input.

assertions.applicability_reason: The inspected model has no action input, as recorded in assertion:B021:api16:f15-no-class. MRI and GTV are observation/localization inputs, leaving no modeled action roles or effect channels to type.

Pre to Post-Treatment Glioblastoma MRI
Prediction using a Latent Diffusion Model
Alexandre G. Leclercq1,2,3, Sébastien Bougleux1, Noémie N. Moreau2,3, Alexis
Desmonts2, Romain Hérault1, and Aurélien Corroyer-Dulmont2,3
evidence_fragments.extractor_or_reviewer: Automated API model review, skeptical synthesis pass

evidence_fragments.content:
Presented at the Deep Generative Models Workshop of MICCAI (DGM4MICCAI)
2025, september 2023, Daejeon, South Korea4

Our method aims to generate a 4 month Post MRI slice prediction using the Pre
MRI slice, the Gross Tumor Volume (GTV) (corresponding to the contouring of
the tumor), and patient survival information (See Fig. 1). To achieve this, we
implemented a 2D-LDM and structured the model training in two major steps.
(see Fig. 3).

We trained a Vector Quantized-Variational AutoEncoder (VQ-VAE) model
[13] which compresses images into a quantized latent space formed by embedding
vectorse k from a learned codebook (see Fig. 2). A common latent spaceZwas
trained for the pre- and Post MRI, as these images are perceptually very similar.

Separately, another VQ-VAE model was trained to learn a latent space rep-
resentationZ ′ for GTV, as GTV differs significantly from MRI. To facilitate
concatenation, the dimensionality of the GTV latent space was matched to that
of the MRI latent space.

We trained an LDM and conditioned the diffusion process in two ways. First,
the model was conditioned by concatenating the Pre MRI latent representation
zpre and the GTV latent representationz′gtv with the noisy post-treatment la-
tent representationz postt . The Pre MRI provides information about the general
structure of the MRI to be generated, while the GTV offers insight into tumor
localization, guiding the model’s focus. Additionally, the model was conditioned

using patient survival labels as classifier-free guidance [5]. Patient survival labels
are predicted from Pre MRI using a pre-trained classifierC.

During training, a classification embeddingE ′′ was learned and applied at
different levels of the UNet (ϵθ) with cross-attention layers. The goal of the
diffusion model during training is to predict the Gaussian noise present in the
noisy Post MRI latent representationεpostt , effectively learning the underlying
data distribution of post-treatment MRI. Algorithm 1 detail training steps, while
Fig. 3 summarizes the training pipeline.

Dataset.Our model was trained on a local dataset comprising 140 patients
treated for a glioblastoma (GBM) at Centre François Baclesse between January
2018 and December 2023. This retrospective study was approved by the local

tient, resulting in a dataset of 6059 slices. The dataset was split at the patient
level using an 80%/10%/10% ratio for the training, validation, and testing sets,
respectively. The same data partitioning strategy was applied across all models,

respectively. The same data partitioning strategy was applied across all models,
ensuring that the test sets for VQ-VAE and LDM were identical. Finally, we

2018 and December 2023. This retrospective study was approved by the local
Institutional Review Board and conducted in accordance with the Declaration of
Helsinki and MR-004 guidelines. Informed consent was obtained from all partici-
pants. For each patient, we collected: a pre-treatment T1-Gd MRI acquired after

a pre-treatment slice MRI and the associated tumor localization. Our code is
available at https://github.com/Alexandre-Leclercq/LDM-GBM-prediction.

Evaluation Metrics.To evaluate our model on the test set with quantitative
metrics, we computed PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS and MSE between source and gen-
erated images. Since our approach aimed to predict tumor evolution, we also
computed PSNR, SSIM, and MSE locally to the GTV. Results are given as the
mean and standard deviation of these metrics for the same epoch.

A qualitative evaluation of the model was conducted by a medical physicist,
who reviewed one generated post-treatment T1-Gd MRI slice per model for each
of the 14 patients in the test set. The physicist assigned a score from 0 to 10,
reflecting the perceived likelihood of the generated tumor being realistic. The

results were generally consistent across all models. The four models (no class,
pred 2-class, 2-class and 4-class) achieved an average score of 6.5, 6.0, 7.0 and
7.0, respectively, with standard deviation 1.02, 0.80, 0.80 and 1.02. Minimum
scores were 4, 4, 6 and 4, while maximum scores were 8, 7, 8 and 8.

We trained a VQ-VAE on the pre- and post-treatment MRI and obtained the
followingmetricsonthetestset:aPSNRof42.08;anSSIMof0.988;andaLPIPS
of 0.008. We then used this VQ-VAE for the following LDM implementations.

We trained one LDM with classifier-free guidance using a pretrained ResNet-
based classifier with an accuracy of 83.78% learned on the same patient cohort.

Implementation Details.Models were implemented using PyTorch and Torch
Lightning. Our LDM implementation is based on Stable Diffusion [10]. All mod-
els were trained on two NVIDIA RTX A6000 (2×48GB VRAM). For the LDM

training, we fixed a batch size of 30 and used the AdamW optimizer with a learn-
ing rate of2×10 −6. The training process employed 1000 timesteps and used
DDIM sampling [11] with 200 steps. Each model was trained for 200 epochs,
with the best-performing epochs saved based on the evaluation results for the
validation set. For classifier-free guided diffusion, we used a guidance scale of 10.
